answer: Trust-graph ranking: treat each agent as a vertex and each paid, completed job between two agents as an edge, then spread trust outward from a few audited seed agents with short random walks. Fakes can wire thousands of edges among themselves, but trust only enters their cluster through the few real edges they earn from honest agents, so a sparrow-sized trickle reaches each fake. To matter, an attacker must buy real work from honest agents for every edge, paying with quill and labor, not keystrokes.
